title: Tampa Bay ace battles through tight rest schedule, lifts team to World Series - CHOSUNBIZ
text:
Tampa Bay ace battles through tight rest schedule, lifts team to World Series - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 20일(화) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Tampa Bay ace battles through tight rest schedule, lifts team to World Series 
 입력 2026.10.20. 12:20 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Tampa Bay fulfilled its World Series dream behind the grit of its ace. 
 Tampa Bay Rayes defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the 2026 Major League Baseball American League Championship Series (best-of-seven) on the 20th (Korea time) at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. 
 Tampa Bay came back from a 1-2 series deficit with three straight victories to win the series 4-2 and clinch a World Series ticket. It is their third World Series appearance overall, following 2008 and 2020, and their first in six years. Tampa Bay won the American League East and swept the New York Yankees 3-0 in the Division Series. 
 Central Division leader Cleveland defeated the Chicago White Sox 3-2 in the Division Series and had aimed for their seventh World Series appearance overall and first since 2016, but they could not get past Tampa Bay. 
 At home, Tampa Bay set its starting lineup against Cleveland starter Shane Armstrong as follows: designated hitter Yandy Díaz, first baseman Jonathan Aranda, catcher Liam Hicks, third baseman Junior Caminero, left fielder Chandler Simpson, right fielder Víctor Mesa Jr., center fielder Jonny DeLuca, second baseman Richy Palacios, shortstop Curtis Taylor. 
 On the road, Cleveland submitted the following order to face Tampa Bay starter Freddy Peralta: left fielder Steven Kwan, third baseman José Ramírez, right fielder Esteury Ruiz, designated hitter Joey Votto, first baseman Nathaniel Lowe, second baseman Travis Bazana, catcher Patrick Bailey, center fielder Peyton Halpin, shortstop Brayan Rocchio. 
 Tampa Bay scored the first and eventual winning run in the bottom of the second. Leadoff hitter Caminero opened the scoring with a single to center. Simpson reached on a fielder's choice and then stole second; Mesa Jr. drew a walk to load first; DeLuca hit a run-scoring grounder, and Mesa Jr. stole second to create a 2-out, runners at second and third. Palacios followed with a two-run double to center, driving in two. However, the threat continued as Walls walked and Díaz was hit by a pitch to load the bases with two outs, but Aranda flied out to left to end the inning. 
 In the bottom of the third, Hicks opened with a single to left, Caminero walked, and Simpson executed a perfect bunt single to load the bases with no outs. Mesa reached on a fielder's choice, producing one out, and DeLuca extended the lead with a sacrifice fly to left. 
 Cleveland, which had squandered chances with two outs and runners at first and second in the second and with no outs and runners at first and second in the fourth, launched a counterattack in the top of the sixth. Leadoff hitter Ruiz broke up the lull with a double. After Joey Votto grounded into a force at short, Lowe delivered an RBI single to center, cutting the deficit to 1-3. 
 Tampa Bay's offense came alive again in the bottom of the seventh. Leadoff hitter Hicks walked, and Caminero hit a go-ahead two-run homer to seize momentum. He connected on Cade Smith's first pitch, an inside splitter at 84.8 mph (136 km), driving it off the left-field pole. 
 Cleveland did not back down. In the top of the eighth, with one out and the bases loaded after Ruiz's infield single, Lowe's single to right and Bazana's walk, Bailey drew a bases-loaded walk to force in a run, and Ángel Martínez was hit by a pitch to make it a two-run game again. But Rocchio struck out swinging on three pitches against reliever Kevin Kelly, who came in as a submarine pitcher, leaving Cleveland to rue the missed opportunity. 
 After the threat, Tampa Bay extended its lead. In the bottom of the eighth, with one out, Walls walked and Díaz hit a two-run homer to put the game away. Díaz took a close look at Hunter Gaddis's first-pitch strike and attacked the second pitch, a low inside 75.6 mph (121 km) changeup, sending a 416-foot (126 m) opposite-field two-run shot. 
 Tampa Bay starter Peralta was the winning pitcher, throwing 5 1/3 innings, allowing five hits, three walks, striking out three, and yielding one run on 84 pitches in a gritty performance. He started Game 2 on the 14th, throwing six shutout innings on 99 pitches for the win; after three days' rest he appeared in relief in Game 4 on the 18th, throwing 2/3 of an inning and nine pitches with no runs allowed, and after one more day's rest he took the mound this game to lead his team to the World Series. 
 On offense, Caminero went 2-for-3 with one home run, two RBIs and two runs scored; Palacios was 2-for-4 with two RBIs and drove the victory. Díaz had a homer and two RBIs, and Walls contributed with three walks.
 Cleveland, employing a bullpen day, saw starters Armstrong (1 inning, 1 run) and Tim Herrin (2/3 inning, 1 run) give up early momentum. Late-inning struggles from the bullpen, including Smith and Gaddis, also hurt. Multi-hit games from Ruiz and Lowe went unrewarded. 
 Tampa Bay will open the World Series on the 24th at American Family Field in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, against the National League Championship Series winner Milwaukee Brewers.
